title: Elastic micro-slice lanes with decay-based KV shedding for low-latency SLO tenants
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: Implement an SLO-aware preemption policy that gives strict low-latency tenants micro-level guarantees while preserving overall throughput via an elastic micro-slice lane system and a decay-based KV shedding mechanism. This ticket covers design, prototype, and short rollout (canary) of the policy plus required telemetry and safety fallbacks.

Background:
- Continuous batching currently improves throughput but can cause head-of-line latency spikes for small, SLO-sensitive requests when large KV-resident working sets occupy GPU memory.
- Existing preemption approaches are coarse (tenant-level time slice steals or full batch preemptors) and either reduce throughput or thrash KV caches.

Success metrics (targets):
- P95 latency for 'low-latency' tenants <= 120ms on 95% of samples under mixed workload (baseline 200ms).
- No more than 7% throughput regression for background workloads at 95th percentile compared to baseline.
- KV cache churn (evictions/sec) increase <= 20% during normal operation vs baseline.

Design summary:
1) Micro-slice lanes: segregate GPU time into micro-slices (~5-40ms) that can be quickly yielded. Lanes are logical QoS bands:
   - Fast lane: prioritized for low-latency tenants with small batch windows and tight preemptibility.
   - Elastic lane: for batch-heavy tenants that can absorb brief preemptions.
   - Bulk lane: for throughput-optimized jobs with longer slices and lower preemption frequency.
   Scheduling then becomes lane-aware: admission picks a lane based on tenant SLO profile and current KV residency.

2) Decay-based KV shedding: instead of wholesale eviction when memory pressure appears, we apply a decayed score per KV resident based on: time-since-last-access, token-weighted contribution to expected future reuse (model-aware heuristic), and tenant priority decay. Shedding proceeds in micro-batches synchronized with slice boundaries to reduce fragmentation.

3) Soft credits & decay: tenants accumulate soft preemption credits based on historical SLO adherence and recent resource usage. Credits decay exponentially (tau configurable) so tenants can recover quickly after heavy bursts. Credits affect lane admission and KV protected-set size.

4) Cooperative yield and preemption lanes: when a Fast-lane request arrives and the GPU is occupied by Elastic/Bulk slices, the runtime attempts cooperative yield at the next micro-slice boundary. If the occupying slice rejects (e.g., non-interruptible kernel), the runtime performs a lightweight interrupt (checkpoint-free) that:
   - pauses decoding/computation at next op boundary, materializes minimal register/stack state, and saves active KV pointers to a fast resume slab in DRAM.

5) Graceful KV protection: tenants with active Fast-lane assignments get a small protected KV budget. If pressure exceeds the protected budget, decay-based shedding reduces lower-scoring residents first; eviction hysteresis mitigates oscillation.

Instrumentation & telemetry:
- New metrics: micro_slice_latency_ms (per-lane), kv_shed_rate, kv_residency_per_tenant, soft_credits (per-tenant), preempt_count_by_type.
- Traces: trace preemption path including cooperative yields, interrupt latencies, and resume times.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (dev): implement simulation harness and unit tests for shedding heuristic (2 weeks).
- Phase 2 (staging canary): enable Fast/Elastic lanes on a small dedicated pool, collect telemetry and compare SLO/throughput targets (2 weeks).
- Phase 3 (gradual rollout): expand to 10% of production traffic with auto-fallback to existing preemptor on regressions (2 weeks).

Risk & mitigations:
- Risk: aggressive shedding might cause model quality regressions (higher hallucination or repetition) for stateful sessions. Mitigation: add per-tenant quality monitors that track eval prompts; automatic rollback on quality regression.
- Risk: interrupt/resume path latency could be worse than predicted on certain kernels. Mitigation: conservative default micro-slice size, kernel opt detection, and opt-out for non-interruptible kernels.

Alternatives considered:
- Strict tenant time-slices (rejected): simple but causes throughput loss and high KV churn.
- Global LRU eviction (rejected): too blunt; evicts high-value long-tail KV entries.

Open questions:
- tau (decay constant) defaults — experimental values: 30s, 2min, 10min.
- How to map product SLO tiers into lane admission heuristics (automatic mapping vs operator-configured).

Next steps:
- Prototype shedding algorithm in the simulation harness (owner: Ben Torres).
- Create design doc with microbench numbers and kernel-level costs (owner: Clara Jensen).
- Add metric emitters to runtime preempt path (owner: Dev infra).
